title: Investigate and harden policy-election telemetry to prevent variant misassignment and regional flapping
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-24 we experienced a ~45 minute production incident where per-request policy evaluation races caused the serving layer to pick an incompatible model variant for requests originating in eu-west-1. The incompatible variant used a quantization profile not supported by the local GPU pool, causing model load errors and a surge of cross-region reroutes. The reroutes then hit a transient policy-state flip which caused region-to-region bounce (flapping) for a subset of sessions, amplifying load and producing increased 5xx and latency for affected customers. Impact: - Visible SLO breaches for latency and error rate for ~2% of requests routed through smart-routing during the window. - Several enterprise customers reported degraded experiences for chat endpoints; support created ~8 tickets. - Automated autoscale reacted but was insufficient before mitigation.

Timeline (high level): - 2026-02-24T10:12 UTC: first spike in routing-error-rate alert (alert routed to oncall). - 2026-02-24T10:13–10:20 UTC: rapid increase in model load failures in eu-west-1 (quant profile mismatch). - 2026-02-24T10:20–10:35 UTC: smart-routing service started cross-region reroutes; policy reconciliation job (periodic background) wrote a policy snapshot concurrently causing stale-to-new decision mismatch. - 2026-02-24T10:30 UTC: observed region-flapping for a subset of session IDs; engineering initiated mitigation. - 2026-02-24T10:35 UTC: mitigation actions (see below) applied; error rates steadily declined and normal routing resumed by 10:57 UTC.

Detection and observability gaps: - Decision-level telemetry was too coarse: we logged final route but not the per-step policy-evaluation decisions (no vector of candidate variants and the reason pourquoi). - No deterministic request-id correlation between the background policy reconciler and in-flight evaluations, so replaying the exact sequence was difficult. - The policy service did not expose a monotonic election counter or decision TTL that could be inspected by downstream services.

Root cause (technical): A race between (A) per-request live policy evaluation that picks a variant candidate based on recent capacity signals and (B) a periodic policy-reconciliation job that writes a new policy snapshot. Because decisions lacked a stable election ordering and decision logs were insufficient, some requests received variant A (quant profile X) while subsequent reconciliation caused the policy layer to advertise variant B (quant profile Y) with different hardware compatibility. When variant A failed to load on eu-west-1 hardware, the routing fallback logic attempted a regional reroute. The reroute triggered another policy evaluation that, due to inconsistent state and missing TTLs, could pick a different target, leading to bounce between regions until decision state converged. The missing guards were: no policy-election mutex/compare-and-swap, lacking decision provenance in logs, and fallback routing allowed immediate cross-region retries without exponential backoff or circuit break.

Immediate mitigation applied during incident: - Reverted the recent routing-policy change that expanded variant selection weightings. - Temporarily disabled cross-region automatic fallback for the affected customers/tenants. - Forced a TTL reset for sticky route caches to clear inconsistent state. - Increased autoscale headroom in eu-west-1 to reduce load while routing stabilized.

Longer-term fixes proposed below.
action_items: AI-1: Implement deterministic decision-logging: record full candidate list, reason codes, provenance (who/what wrote the decision), and election counter for every evaluated request. Owner: Mei Chen. Due: 2026-03-10.

AI-2: Add compare-and-swap (CAS) semantics to policy-reconciliation writes so background snapshots cannot silently override a live per-request decision without an election check. Owner: Rafael Gomez. Due: 2026-03-17.

AI-3: Enforce a decision TTL and vector-clock on route decisions consumed by the serving layer; include TTL/epoch in routing headers so downstream can reject stale decisions. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-24.

AI-4: Add a regional reroute circuit-breaker with incremental backoff (3 retries with exponential backoff) and an emergency stop that prevents immediate cross-region retries for sessions showing repeated failures. Owner: Jonah Park. Due: 2026-03-10.

AI-5: Create an integration test harness that replays concurrent policy-reconcile and in-flight-eval scenarios (chaos tests) to validate race conditions before rolling policy changes. Owner: SRE Team (Ravi Shah lead). Due: 2026-04-07.

AI-6: Dashboard and alerting: add an 'election-mismatch' metric that counts cases where per-request decision provenance differs from active snapshot owner; wire an SLO alert if rate > 0.1% over 5m. Owner: Observability (Nina Flores). Due: 2026-03-03.
AI-7: Customer communication: drafting post-incident summary for affected customers and support playbook for similar degradations. Owner: Customer Success (Hannah Li). Due: 2026-03-05.
acceptance_criteria: Decision logs emitted for 100% of routing evaluations (prod sampling at 100% for 3 days in canary region).
Policy writes use CAS semantics and unit/integration tests cover CAS failure modes.
Decision TTL and epoch headers are present and validated by serving layer; stale decisions rejected with a specific error code.
Regional reroute circuit-breaker implemented and tested; no session should experience >2 region hops in 10 minutes during chaos tests.
New dashboard metric 'election-mismatch' visible in Console and tied to oncall paging policy.
